# Golden instances: <name>|<solver arguments>
# Fronts are generated by the brute-force oracle (tests/oracle) with
# tests/golden/regenerate.sh. Symmetric durations only, t <= 5 (the oracle is
# exponential: n=6 t=6 p=2 already takes minutes).
# @DATA@ expands to tests/golden/data.
# Names carry the 2016 generator flags. zeno no longer applies the 2016 swap of
# durations and costs, so the arguments are written in the current meaning:
# the 2016 "-C a -D b" is "-C b -D a" (the same instance up to city order).
#
# Default generators (f = g = identity), including the n = t instances of
# Table 1 of Quemy & Schoenauer, EvoCOP 2015 (front sizes 5, 10, 17).
n2t2p1|-n 2 -t 2 -p 1
n3t2p1|-n 3 -t 2 -p 1
n2t3p1|-n 2 -t 3 -p 1
n2t3p2|-n 2 -t 3 -p 2
n3t3p1|-n 3 -t 3 -p 1
n3t3p2|-n 3 -t 3 -p 2
n4t3p2|-n 4 -t 3 -p 2
n3t4p2|-n 3 -t 4 -p 2
n3t4p3|-n 3 -t 4 -p 3
n4t4p2|-n 4 -t 4 -p 2
n4t4p3|-n 4 -t 4 -p 3
n3t5p2|-n 3 -t 5 -p 2
n3t5p3|-n 3 -t 5 -p 3
n5t4p2|-n 5 -t 4 -p 2
n5t4p3|-n 5 -t 4 -p 3
n5t5p2|-n 5 -t 5 -p 2
# Other generating functions and scales.
n3t3p1-C4D3|-n 3 -t 3 -p 1 -C 3 -D 4
n3t4p2-C2D3r10|-n 3 -t 4 -p 2 -r 10 -C 3 -D 2
n4t3p2-C3D5r10|-n 4 -t 3 -p 2 -r 10 -C 5 -D 3
n4t4p2-C4D3|-n 4 -t 4 -p 2 -C 3 -D 4
n4t5p3-C5D2r10|-n 4 -t 5 -p 3 -r 10 -C 2 -D 5
n5t4p3-C4D5|-n 5 -t 4 -p 3 -C 4 -D 5
n3t5p2-C1D4r10|-n 3 -t 5 -p 2 -r 10 -C 4 -D 1
# Two cities, d = (6, 10), c = (40, 20), t = 5, p = 2. The point (260, 60) is
# Pareto-optimal but the greedy of Algorithm 1 (EvoCOP 2015) returns 68 for its
# PPP e = (10,10,6,6,6), w = (10,6,6): A flies 20+20+20, B flies 12*5.
lpt-counterexample|-n 2 -t 5 -p 2 -d @DATA@/lpt-counterexample.dat
# Two cities, d = (1, 9), c = (4, 1), t = 5, p = 3, from a data file that ends
# with a newline and a blank line (it used to be read as a different instance).
trailing-newline|-n 2 -t 5 -p 3 -d @DATA@/trailing-newline.dat
# Same instance without the trailing newline. zenoSolver_noDuplicate used to
# keep the last plan evaluated for a PPP instead of the best one, and reported
# (22, 20) and (25, 18) instead of (13, 36) and (22, 18).
nodup-best-plan|-n 2 -t 5 -p 3 -d @DATA@/nodup-best-plan.dat
# Two cities, d = (1, 3), c = (9, 5), t = 4, p = 2. The point (42, 12) needs a
# P3 through the d = 3 city: A flies the drop-off then east through it (6+6),
# B flies east, west, east through the d = 1 city then the pick-up (2+2+2+6).
# Algorithm 1 finds it. zenoSolver_noDuplicate places the drop-off first and
# then gives the longest first crossing to the other plane, and ends at 14.
p3-first-counterexample|-n 2 -t 4 -p 2 -d @DATA@/p3-first-counterexample.dat
